name: Pet bowl size and height guidance

rules.rule: Rim from elbow height down to 7.5 cm (3 in) below it
rules.evidence: rule of thumb from pet-product guides; no veterinary guideline

rules.rule: Floor, or a rim above 30.5 cm (1 ft) and up to elbow height
rules.evidence: cohort study, 1,637 dogs: GDV per 1,000 dog-years, floor 18, raised 1 ft or less 56 (RR 3.06, 95% CI 1.60-5.87), raised more than 1 ft 29 (not significant)
rules.note: One study with 98 GDV cases, so a guide; an internet survey of 1,114 GDV cases found no clear effect of bowl height. Dogs with megaesophagus are fed from a raised position on purpose, on their vet's plan.

rules.rule: Floor, or a rim at 30.5 cm (1 ft) or lower
rules.evidence: same cohort: GDV per 1,000 dog-years, floor 17, raised 1 ft or less 15 (not significant), raised more than 1 ft 39 (RR 2.29, 95% CI 1.15-4.58)
rules.note: One study with 98 GDV cases, so a guide; an internet survey of 1,114 GDV cases found no clear effect of bowl height. Dogs with megaesophagus are fed from a raised position on purpose, on their vet's plan.

rules.rule: Dish at least as wide as the whisker span
rules.evidence: 38-cat study: no difference in time eating, food dropped or food eaten; 63% of owners said their cat preferred the wide dish

rules.rule: At least 1.5 x the meal volume, 2 x for a slow feeder; 1 US cup = 236.6 ml

Meal volume = cups x 236.6 ml, or grams (1 oz = 28.35 g; a can is its net weight) / the food's grams in one level cup x 236.6 ml, added up over the foods. Grams in one cup: dry food = the maker's kcal per cup / kcal per kg x 1000, or the cup weight on the label; dry food not listed = 86.1 g, the 10th percentile of the 50 listed dry foods; wet food = 236.6 g (1.0 g per ml); fresh-cooked food from the maker (146.5 to 188 g), or 146.5 g when not listed, also for raw and homemade food; freeze-dried 45 g; water or broth 236.6 g
rules.evidence: maker calorie statements (foods.js, one source per food, checked 15 November 2026); density of mostly-water food about 1.05-1.10 g per ml without air (Choi and Okos 1986 composition model), rounded down so the bowl errs big

rules.applies_to: dogs and cats that eat fast
rules.rule: A slow feeder or puzzle feeder lengthens the meal; vets suggest one for large and giant dogs and for pets that gulp and vomit, and puzzle feeders for cats
rules.evidence: 10-dog study: meals took longer, still slower after 9 days; eating fast was a GDV risk factor in two Purdue studies; VCA advises a puzzle feeder or slow-down bowl for large and giant dogs; AAFP consensus recommends puzzle feeders for cats; Veterinary Partner says feeders prevent gulping and may lessen vomiting, and suggests puzzle bowls for dogs that swallow air; no trial of bloat prevention

rules.rule: Size by elbow height, not weight
Narrower opening or a tilted bowl
RER = 70 x kg^0.75 kcal/day; MER = RER x factor (dog: neutered 1.6, intact 1.8, inactive 1.2-1.4, growth 2-3; cat: neutered 1.2, intact 1.4, inactive 1.0, growth 2-3); cups = MER / kcal per cup
rules.evidence: Pet Nutrition Alliance table; estimates only, pets can vary by as much as 50%, adjust to body condition

rules.rule: Choose a food labelled complete and balanced for the life stage; for puppies that will be large dogs, the label should include growth of large size dogs
rules.evidence: label rule; large-breed puppies need tighter calcium limits
